observations: Photo 0: A dark blue iPhone with a triple-camera setup and a large camera module. The back has stickers and a white label with a barcode and partial text 'iPhone 13 Pro Max'.

Photo 1: The front screen is on, showing iOS with widgets and app icons. The notch is visible, and the screen appears to be in good condition. The phone is held in a hand, with reflections from a glass display case.
Photo 2: Same as photo 0, showing the back of the phone with the same stickers and label. The label text is partially obscured but appears to read 'iPhone 13 Pro Max'.
All photos show the phone in a retail environment with other phones in display cases in the background.
The seller claims it is an 'iPhone 17 Promax', but the label and design match an iPhone 13 Pro Max.
The phone is described as 'UK used', '1TB', 'eSIM unlocked', and available in 'white and orange', but only one blue phone is shown.

claims.evidence: The label on the back of the phone in photo 0 and photo 2 clearly reads 'iPhone 13 Pro Max'. The design, including the camera module and notch, matches the iPhone 13 Pro Max, not the non-existent iPhone 17 Pro Max.
The phone appears clean in the photos, but there is no close-up of the screen, edges, or ports to verify condition. Scratches or wear could be hidden.

No proof of origin or usage history is visible. The label and stickers appear to be in Chinese, suggesting a different origin. No UK-specific identifiers (like IMEI, warranty, or packaging) are shown.

The storage capacity cannot be confirmed from the photos. The label does not show storage size. The iPhone 13 Pro Max does not come in 1TB; the max is 1TB only for iPhone 15 Pro Max and later models. This claim is likely false.
No proof of eSIM functionality or carrier unlock status is visible. The phone is on, but no settings or carrier info is shown.
Only one blue phone is shown in all photos. No other colors are visible. The claim of availability in white and orange is not supported by the images.

A screenshot of the phone's settings showing carrier status and eSIM unlock status.
Close-up photos of the screen, edges, and ports to verify condition.
A video of the phone turning on, off, and showing the home screen and settings.
